title: MemoryExtractor: automatic LLM-driven memory extraction on message ingest
summary: Pluggable MemoryExtractor protocol (parallel to Consolidator/Reconciler/IngestResolver) wired into add_messages(), opt-in via memory_extractor= and extract_memories= flag.
description:
Oracle's OracleThread.add_messages() automatically extracts durable memories from recent thread messages via a configured LLM, on by default (extract_memories=True), with an explicit opt-out. This SDK has no equivalent — the existing Consolidator processes raw working/episodic writes generically, and PIPE-2's IngestResolver classifies a candidate the caller already decided to write; neither triggers automatically from add_messages() itself.

Add a MemoryExtractor Protocol to types.py (parallel in shape and docstring style to Consolidator/Reconciler/IngestResolver): (messages: list[WorkingMemory], scope) -> list[_MemoryBase]. Ship NoOpMemoryExtractor. Add memory_extractor= constructor param on MemoryStore (default NoOp) and extract_memories: bool = True on add_messages(). When enabled with a real extractor configured, derived records are remembered through the existing remember() path (so PIPE-2/ENH-2 already apply). Extractor errors are caught and logged, never propagated.

Depends on THRD-1 (needs add_messages() to exist as the hook point) — do not start until THRD-1 is merged. Independent of THRD-2/3/4.
